neighbours.label: A court or reporter abbreviation inside a formal legal citation (11th Cir., F.2d, S.D.N.Y., supra note), not the same case discussed in plain prose
fire: See United States v. Brown, 412 F.3d 1201, 1205 (9th Cir. 2005).
The rule was applied in Lopez v. City of Dallas, 77 F.2d 18 (5th Cir. 1935).
Accord Hanson v. Reed, 905 F.2d 112, 115 (2d Cir. 1990).
Cf. Ortiz v. Price, 201 F. Supp. 2d 44, 49 (S.D.N.Y. 2002).
But see Keller v. Grant, 618 F.3d 900, 904 (7th Cir. 2010).
The panel followed Walsh v. Ford, 33 F.4th 87, 92 (1st Cir. 2022).
See generally Park v. Moore, 140 F.3d 560 (D.C. Cir. 1998).
Id.; see also Diaz v. Hale, 512 F.3d 77, 81 (3d Cir. 2008).
quiet: The federal appeals court in San Francisco sided with Brown in 2005.
The rule was applied when Lopez sued the City of Dallas in the 1930s.
Hanson and Reed settled their dispute out of court in 1990.
Ortiz lost his case against Price in a New York trial court.
Keller argued that Grant had broken the contract years earlier.
The judges in Boston agreed with Walsh on most points.
Park and Moore disagreed about the meaning of the statute.
Diaz and Hale both appealed after the verdict was announced.
